column4: A small 1998 palmtop computer vibrating twice inside a canvas trouser pocket: two short muffled buzzing rattles against keys and fabric, close, quiet, outdoors. No beeps, no music.
A small plastic palmtop computer giving one short low error buzz from its tiny speaker, a cheap electronic burr, close, dry. No music.
A plastic stylus tapping once on the hard resistive touch screen of an old palmtop computer: a tiny dry click of plastic on plastic, very close. Nothing else.
One tiny high electronic beep from the piezo speaker of a 1990s pocket computer, short and thin, close, dry. Nothing else.
Pulling a small plastic palmtop computer out of a canvas jacket pocket and flipping its cover open: a soft fabric rustle and a light plastic snap, close. No beeps.

An old village public address system chime before an announcement: three slow descending electronic gong tones, ding dong dang, played through a horn loudspeaker on a pole, outdoors, a short echo off the woods. No voice, no music.

A man reading a short announcement through a distant crackling village loudspeaker on a pole across a field, the words completely unintelligible, muffled, distorted and echoing, with the hiss of an old amplifier. No music.
A woman reading a short notice through a faraway old public address horn in a holiday camp, the words not understandable, tinny and echoing, with crackle and hum. No music.

The steady hum of an old beige 1998 desktop computer running in a quiet small office: the power supply fan whirring, the hard disk spinning with a faint high whine, close, constant, no clicks, no beeps, no music.
A few quick quiet clicks and ticks of an old desktop computer hard disk seeking data, close, in a quiet room. Nothing else.

A 1990s dot-matrix printer printing two short lines in a quiet small office: the print head buzzing and screeching across and back, the paper advancing with a plastic ratchet click, close. Nothing else, no music.
